A view is not a copy of your data. It is a named query plus a rendering configuration, stored as JSON. Change the view
type and the same entities appear as a kanban board, a timeline, a graph or a masonry feed; the records stay where
they are.

## View types

The view types a pod implements are defined in `packages/types/src/renderables/views.ts` of the backend repository.
19 are implemented:

| Category | View types |
|---|---|
| Structured | `sheet`, `table`, `list`, `grid`, `gallery`, `kanban`, `matrix`, `masonry`, `calendar`, `gantt`, `timeline`, `graph`, `flow`, `map`, `zoom_map` |
| Canvas | `whiteboard` |
| Special | `pipeline`, `branch_tree`, `bento` |

Not every implemented type can be created as a new view: `table` (superseded by `sheet`), `branch_tree` (only
meaningful inside a conversation), `zoom_map` (retired as a new view) and `pipeline` (created by its own flows) remain
renderable for existing views but are not offered when you create one. `mindmap` is defined but not implemented.

New view types are adapters in the view renderer; the data layer does not change.

## Views created by agents

Because a view is configuration, an agent can create one from a request in plain language, for example:

- "Create a pipeline view of my deals grouped by stage": a kanban configuration with `groupBy: dealStage`.
- "Build a team dashboard with open tasks, recent activity and deal velocity": a bento configuration with three
  widget blocks.
- "Show me a graph of how my contacts relate to each other": a graph view configuration.

The agent writes the configuration and the view renderer draws it.
